links.note: Speed of a toy, exponential-time index calculus; the measurement quantifies its distance to rho, it cannot establish a speedup.

question: On the registered bench-roster prime-order curves of 10, 12, 14 and 16 bits, what does the tensor-contraction index calculus (ic.tensor_contraction_v1, m = 2) cost in counted operations S and in L2 wall time, against the matched rho.negation reference and the prime-curve ic.pipeline baseline, and how does its cost scale with r?

claims.text: Every measured row of every arm recovers the planted scalar (verified by the harness).
Per curve, the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-m2 over rho-neg, with its bootstrap interval and the §5a band (unpriced native work at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation on every arm).
claims.if_supported: a measured gap to rho on these four curves; no claim beyond them
claims.if_not_supported: the ratio interval includes 1 or the order flips inside the §5a band: no ranking

claims.text: Per curve, the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-m2 over ic-mitm (the existing prime-curve IC baseline), with the §5a band.
claims.if_supported: a measured difference from the IC baseline on these curves
claims.if_not_supported: no ranking against the IC baseline

claims.text: The log-log slope of median S of tensor-m2 against log2 r over the four sizes, reported descriptively with the four points.
claims.if_supported: a fitted exponent on four toy sizes, labelled an extrapolation outside them

claims.text: Per curve of the main session (10, 12, 14 bits), the L2 wall-time ratio tensor-m2 over rho-neg, only where ecbench compare admits wall time and it is outside the A/A noise. The A/A comparison C-aa supplies the noise floor.
claims.if_supported: an admitted wall-time gap on these curves
claims.if_not_supported: wall time quoted as descriptive or not at all

hypotheses.statement: The tensor arm costs far more than rho in S on every curve, and the gap grows with r.
hypotheses.mechanism: Each relation is found by exact contraction costing about |F_1||F_2| ≈ 2r point additions, and N + 1 ≈ 2(2r)^(1/2) relations are needed, so total GAE grows like r^(3/2) and S = GAE/sqrt(r) like r; rho's S is about 1.

predictions.minimum_effect: ratio interval above 1 on every curve, increasing from 8 to 14 bits

positive.not_applicable_reason: every workload carries a planted scalar and the harness checks [k]G = Q on every row; a miss is a wrong_answer row

negative.not_applicable_reason: a cost comparison between methods on the same instances asserts nothing about a null population

factors.name: curve
factors.value: prime_roster 10, 12, 14 (main session) and 16 (counts-only session); registered ICV1 slugs icv1-fp10-t5-192cb216, icv1-fp12-t19-d4a315df, icv1-fp14-tm43-158b6914, icv1-fp16-t351-d433f24e
factors.how: every arm runs every curve; comparisons are per curve

factors.name: targets
factors.how: the spec's target law, independent of arm

factors.name: binary
factors.value: one ecbench binary built from the source commit the EKS image is built from

factors.name: algorithm_seed
factors.how: derived per execution by the harness from measurement.seed 20261030, independent of arm; the 16-bit session uses the same seed

factors.name: host_load
factors.how: steal, PSI, foreign busy ticks per row; affects wall time only

randomization.arm_order_reason: main session: alternate over 6 measured rounds (balanced); 16-bit session: alternate_measured over its single round, which ecbench cannot balance; that session's metric is counted S, which arm order does not affect

seed_derivation.note: ecbench derives algorithm_seed per execution from measurement.seed 20261030 and the plan

instance_sampling.rule: 8 targets per curve from target_seed 20261030 under the spec's target law, in both sessions

blinding.how: not masked: arms are named by method in the harness output; the decision rule is fixed below before data

power.note: main session: 8 workloads x 6 rounds = 48 paired observations per arm per curve; 16-bit session: 8 workloads x 1 round (S is deterministic per run); the expected effect is far outside any plausible interval width

preflight_runtime.measured_on: descriptive single tensor solves on this container: 12 bits 3 s, 14 bits 21 s, 16 bits 417 s (contended host); rho and ic.pipeline are sub-second

primary.name: S
primary.definition: every phase charged in ecbench.gae divided by sqrt(r)

secondary.name: unpriced native work
secondary.definition: each arm's *_uncharged counters, priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation for the §5a band

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: main session 4 arms x 24 workloads x (1 warmup + 6 rounds) = 672 executions; 16-bit session 4 arms x 8 workloads x (1 warmup + 1 round) = 64 executions; then stop
a row whose answer does not verify stops nothing and is recorded as wrong_answer

invalidation_rules: a row with outcome.status other than verified is excluded from the decisive comparison and reported
a wall-time value on a row below L2 is descriptive only; counted units stand at any level
a session whose audit is not OK with every replay identical yields no result
the 16-bit session carries no wall-time claim at any isolation level

decision_rule.text: Per curve, C2 (C3) is supported when the paired ratio of summed S tensor-m2 over rho-neg (ic-mitm) has a 95% bootstrap interval excluding 1 and the order holds at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per unpriced operation on every arm; otherwise no ranking on that curve. C5 needs ecbench compare to admit wall time and report outside_noise true. Holm correction over the family of per-curve comparisons; C-aa is the noise floor, not a decision.
decision_rule.threshold: ratio interval excludes 1 across the §5a band
decision_rule.statistic: sum of S over (workload, round) pairs, ratio candidate/reference (ecbench compare)
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per curve

graphs: median S per arm against log2 r, per curve, with intervals
L2 wall time per arm per curve where admitted

inadmissible: changing the workloads, seeds, unit or accounting after seeing results
quoting wall time from rows below L2 or not outside the A/A noise as a result
reading a toy-size measurement as evidence about deployed curves
calling any result a speedup: the counters are exponential

literature.claim: the counted unit S, isolation levels and paired comparison
the algorithm, its exponential counters and its limits
